Lamar Bunting and Gene Neumeier caught a winning 9.12 pounds with five fish. Their best fish measured 2.37 pounds. (updated 11-12-2026) Marsha Robinson at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said the lake’s surface water temperature is tumbling and falling as low as 60.4 degrees earlier this week. Catfish are all that she heard about this past week; there were no reports on bream, crappie or bass. Catfish have been excellent both on cut bait and blood bait. Most of the catches are coming on jigs or limbline

(updated 10-29-2026) The AGFC Fisheries Division had an update on fishing Lake Poinsett as we hate into the last third of fall. The foliage is in perfect splendor, cooler temperatures are here, and there are some great fishing opportunities to be had. Since its renovation and reopening in 2022, Lake Poinsett has developed an impressive fishery for redear sunfish (commonly called “shellcrackers").

(updated 11-5-2026) Mark Crawford with springriverfliesandguides.com (870-955-8300) said water level remains low with clear water clarity. The area remains very dry with record low water levels. It’s a great time for small-stream fishing with the low water. Search out deeper pools and riffles and tail-out pockets below riffles. (updated 11-12-2026) Shelley Burr at Cane Creek State Park, (870-628-4714) reported most recently that the lake is very low and overrun with lily pads. Few anglers were venturing out. Cane Creek Lake is a 1,700-acre lake in Lincoln County that was built in 1986 and is owned and managed by the AGFC. It is stocked with bass, crappie, bream and catfish.
